title: Graph Systems of Linear Inequalities
student_objective: I can graph a system of two linear inequalities and identify the overlapping solution region.

concept_cards.title: Graph each inequality separately
concept_cards.content: For each inequality, graph its boundary line with the correct solid/dashed style and shade its solution half-plane.

concept_cards.title: The overlap is the system solution
concept_cards.content: A point solves the system only if it satisfies both inequalities, so the final answer is the region where the two shadings overlap.

concept_cards.title: Boundary inclusion matters
concept_cards.content: A point on a boundary is included only if that inequality uses ≤ or ≥ and therefore has a solid boundary.

concept_cards.title: Test a point in the overlap
concept_cards.content: To verify your final region, choose a sample point inside it and check that the point makes both inequalities true.

overlap.teacher_signal: Student shades the union instead of the overlap.

verify.teacher_signal: Student does not verify that points satisfy both inequalities.

items.prompt: For a system of two inequalities, should the final solution be the union of all shaded regions or only the overlap?
hint_steps: A solution must satisfy inequality 1 and inequality 2.
So a point must be in both shaded regions.

solution_steps.explanation: The system requires both inequalities to be true.
Only shared shaded points solve the system.

items.prompt: In the inequality y≤x+2, is the boundary line included? Answer yes or no.
items.tutor_behavior: Review boundary inclusion before systems work.

items.prompt: For the system y≥x and y≤-x+4, where is the solution region?
items.tutor_behavior: Model two shadings and their shared wedge.
hint_steps: Keep only the region that is both above the first and below the second.

solution_steps.explanation: Use a solid boundary and shade above.
Use a solid boundary and shade below.
The shared shaded region solves both inequalities.

items.prompt: For y>2x-1 and y<2x+3, describe the solution region and boundary styles.
items.tutor_behavior: Show a band-shaped overlap with strict boundaries.
hint_steps: Both inequalities are strict, so both boundaries are dashed.
y>2x-1 shades above the lower line.
y<2x+3 shades below the upper line, leaving the band between them.

items.prompt: For y≥0 and y≤x+2, describe the overlap.
items.answer_key: above or on the x-axis and below or on y=x+2
accepted_answers: above or on the x-axis and below or on y=x+2
between y=0 and y=x+2 where they overlap
items.tutor_behavior: Use one horizontal boundary and one slanted boundary.
hint_steps: y≤x+2 shades below the slanted line.
The overlap is where both conditions hold.

items.prompt: For y<x+1 and y>-x-1, describe the solution region.
items.tutor_behavior: Model an open wedge with dashed boundaries.
hint_steps: Both inequalities are strict, so both boundaries are dashed.
Shade above y=-x-1; the overlap is between them.

solution_steps.explanation: Only the shared region satisfies both.

items.prompt: Does (0,1) satisfy the system y≥x and y≤-x+2? Answer yes or no.
items.tutor_behavior: Verify an overlap point by substitution into both inequalities.

items.prompt: For y≤2 and y≥-x, describe the solution overlap.
items.answer_key: below or on y=2 and above or on y=-x
accepted_answers: below or on y=2 and above or on y=-x

solution_steps.explanation: The shared region solves the system.

items.prompt: For y>3 and y<x+5, are the boundaries solid or dashed?
items.tutor_behavior: Student applies strict-inequality boundary rule twice.

items.prompt: Does (2,1) satisfy y≤x and y≥-x+1? Answer yes or no.
items.tutor_behavior: Student checks a point against both inequalities.

solution_steps.explanation: The point is in the overlap.

items.prompt: For y≥x-2 and y≤x+4, describe the solution region.
hint_steps: Both use equality, so both lines are solid.
Shade below y=x+4, leaving the band between.

items.prompt: For y<0 and y>2x-6, describe the overlap.
items.answer_key: below the x-axis and above y=2x-6
accepted_answers: below the x-axis and above y=2x-6
items.tutor_behavior: Mastery check with two strict boundaries.
hint_steps: y>2x-6 shades above the slanted line.
Both boundaries are dashed and the overlap is between them where both conditions hold.

items.prompt: Does (1,2) satisfy y≥x+1 and y≤3? Answer yes or no.
A point lies in the shaded region of the first inequality but not the second. Is it a solution of the system?
items.tutor_behavior: Reinforce that systems require both conditions.
hint_steps: A system means both inequalities must be true.
Therefore it is not a system solution.

solution_steps.explanation: The point is outside the overlap.

items.prompt: Why is the overlap of two shaded half-planes the solution set of a system of inequalities?
items.answer_key: because every point in the overlap satisfies both inequalities
accepted_answers: because every point in the overlap satisfies both inequalities
points in the overlap make both inequalities true
hint_steps: Each shaded region represents one inequality's solutions.
A system requires both inequalities at once.
Only points in the overlap satisfy both.

solution_steps.explanation: The system solution is the intersection of the two solution sets.
Every point there satisfies both inequalities.
